extracted.intended_audience: ARIPO Search and Examination Section examiners / patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting searches, preparing search reports, and classifying ARIPO patent applications, including handling lack of unity, excluded subject-matter, pre-/official classification, and post-search procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include all claim categories in the search
rubrics_metrics.description: When the application contains claims of different categories, all these must be included in the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if a product claim clearly seems to be both new and non-obvious, the examiner need not specially search claims for a process which inevitably results in manufacture of that product or for use of the product. When the application contains only claims of one category, it may be desirable to include other categories in the search. Example (chemical process): starting products may be assumed part of the state of the art and need not be searched; intermediate products are searched only when claimed; final products will always be searched except when evidently known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter excluded from search (Section 3(10)(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may exclude certain subject-matter from the search where exclusions arise from the Harare Protocol, national laws, or where meaningful search is impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions may result from patentability exclusions or inability to conduct a meaningful search (e.g. severe non-compliance with Harare Protocol or Rule 7 bis.3). Any such exclusions must be indicated in the search report or declaration with reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction of search due to lack of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims do not relate to one invention or a group linked to form a single general inventive concept, the search will normally be restricted to the invention or linked group first mentioned in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction is notified to applicant in communication accompanying the partial search report; the partial search report must be supplemented with specification of the separate inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include technological background when desirable
rubrics_metrics.description: In certain circumstances extend search to include the 'technological background' of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technological background includes: the preamble to the first claim (part preceding 'characterized by' / 'characterized in that'), the state of the art noted in the description introduction but not specifically cited, and the general technological background ('general state of the art').

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of the application prior to searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Before searching, the examiner should consider the application to determine the subject of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a critical analysis of claims in light of description and drawings: identify the underlying problem, inventive concept, features essential to the solution, and results/effects. Include in the search technical features indicated in the description as essential even if not present in the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify formal deficiencies but avoid duplicating Formality Section
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner notices formal shortcomings overlooked by the Formality Section, raise them via internal communication, but do not repeat or undertake time-consuming formality enquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of deficiencies: missing paper/electronic sequence listing; incorrect page numbering; drawings present in description/claims; erasures/alterations jeopardizing authenticity; prohibited matter (ordre public, disparaging statements); failures in biological deposit identification; failure to identify divisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine documents cited in the application when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents cited in the application should be examined if they are the starting point of the invention, show the state of the art, give alternative solutions, or are necessary for correct understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations clearly relating only to irrelevant details may be disregarded. If a cited document is unpublished or inaccessible and appears essential, invite the applicant to submit it or indicate subject-matter to be searched; absence may lead to incomplete search report with stated grounds. If applicant later furnishes the document, an additional search may be carried out under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine abstract, title, classification for publication before search
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the abstract, title and drawing (if any) for publication and relation to Implementing Regulations before carrying out the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine abstract content before search to avoid being influenced by search results. If application will be published before the search report is drawn up, establish official classification and examine abstract earlier. Ensure abstract relates to the application and does not conflict with title or classification; transmit related information to the applicant in the communication accompanying the search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare a precise search statement and note necessary restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a search statement defining the subject of the search as precisely as possible (claims may need generalization to cover all aspects/embodiments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bear in mind subjects excluded from patentability and lack of unity. If restrictions are necessary because meaningful search is impossible, indicate them in the search report or declaration with reasons; such declaration or incomplete report is considered the search report for subsequent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulate an iterative, interactive search strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate a search strategy as a plan of search statements expressing the subject and resulting in documentation sections to consult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial strategy contains combinations of basic claim components. Reformulate according to retrieved information. When using classification units, select units in directly relevant and analogous fields, limited to (i) higher subdivisions for abstraction and (ii) parallel subdivisions mindful of unrelatedness. Request advice from Principal Examiner when in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize search strategies with highest probability of relevant documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Select search strategies yielding sections where probability of finding highly relevant documents is highest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precedence to main technical field of the application, starting with basic components most relevant to specific examples and preferred embodiments. Use examiner judgment based on experience and available search tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on documents relevant for novelty and inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: During the search direct attention to documents relevant for novelty and inventive step, and note documents important for other reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other reasons include conflicting documents (published ARIPO, international, national applications; documents published during priority interval), documents putting doubt on priority (L), documents aiding understanding (T), technological background (A), ARIPO applications relevant to double patenting (L), internet documents lacking publication dates (L). Do not spend significant time searching for these unless special reason exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuously reformulate search subject based on results
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuously evaluate search results and reformulate the subject as necessary (e.g., change classification units or their search order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider consulting documents cited in relevant documents or documents citing relevant documents. Exercise caution when searching external collections (Internet) so as not to reveal confidential unpublished patent application material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite closest prior art as an 'A' document
rubrics_metrics.description: If no documents published before the earliest priority date prejudice novelty or inventive step, cite prior art found that discloses a solution to the same problem (closest prior art) as an 'A' document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no such document exists, cite a document solving a closely related problem with technically similar solution. If incidentally retrieved documents are prejudicial to novelty (X) but not inventive step after amendment, proceed similarly. In supplementary ARIPO searches, it is permissible to have no further relevant documents beyond the international search.

rubrics_metrics.name: End search when further discoveries are unlikely or when novelty clearly lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: End the search when probability of discovering further relevant prior art becomes very low relative to effort needed, or when documents clearly demonstrate lack of novelty for the entire subject-matter (except trivial/common general knowledge features).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regardless, search for conflicting applications should always be completed to the extent present in available documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and limit documents cited in the search report
rubrics_metrics.description: After completing the search, select documents to cite in the report, always including the most relevant documents to be specially characterized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite less relevant documents only when they concern aspects not found in already selected documents. In doubtful/borderline cases cite more readily to assist examination. Avoid citing more documents than necessary; when several documents of equal relevance exist normally cite no more than one. Include an annex (computer-drawn) listing patent-family documents; prefer language convenience and cite documents in the language of the application where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add documents discovered after completion up to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents discovered after completion of a search report should be added to the search report up to the time preparations for its publication are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Up to filing of a request for examination, later-discovered documents should be communicated to the applicant as an addition to the search report and will be published. Thereafter, such documents may be used in examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct material errors in the search report and notify applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: When a material error is found in a search report prior to publication a new report superseding the previous one is drawn up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the erroneous report has been sent to the applicant but not yet published, notify the applicant immediately. If a serious error is noted after publication, publish a corrigendum in the ARIPO Patent Journal and inform the applicant and Search and Examination Section; if an incorrect cited document was transmitted, send the correct document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and purpose of pre-classification and official classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-classification is a first routing stage broadly identifying the subject for internal handling; official classification assigns appropriate classification symbols identifying technical subject as precisely/comprehensively as the IPC permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official classification performed by the examiner using Obligatory Classification (IPC). Non-obligatory classification or indexation symbols may be added per the Guide to the IPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-classification (routing) based on independent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Make pre-classification to allot the application to a competent examiner; level should be as general as practicable but specific enough (usually sub-class) to avoid intermediate routing steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-classification should be made on the basis of independent claims. If resulting in more than one sub-class, select whichever seems most relevant to the claimed invention (or the invention first claimed if lack of unity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reclassify and reallocate incorrectly pre-classified applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is found to be incorrectly pre-classified and thus inappropriately allocated, reclassify and re-allocate it and amend the dossier indication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally done by mutual agreement with the receiving section; where disagreement or uncertainty exists consult the Principal Examiner rather than spending time resolving classification boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official classification should relate to the application as filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification should be determined without taking into consideration probable content after amendment and should relate to the disclosure in the published application (as filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner's understanding alters significantly as a result of the search (e.g., due to prior art found or clarification), amend the classification accordingly if preparations for publication have not been completed. If classification spans multiple sub-classes or groups, assign all such classifications and indicate the symbol most adequately identifying the invention first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification when scope of invention not clear
rubrics_metrics.description: When the scope of the invention is not clear (e.g., partial search), classification must be based on what appears to be the invention insofar as it can be understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amend classification later if obscurities are removed by the search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify each invention when there is lack of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where objection of lack of unity arises, all inventions must be classified since all will be disclosed in the published application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each invention claimed is to be classified; classification covers every invention even if a partial search report is prepared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend search when claimed priority dates cannot be verified
rubrics_metrics.description: If claimed priority dates cannot be verified at the classification/search stage, extend the search for conflicting applications to cover all published applications with an earliest claimed priority date up to the filing date of the application under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents missing conflicting art when priority is uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select for citation primarily documents available in search documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: As a general rule, the Search Examiner selects for citation only documents present in the search documentation or accessible by other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use available documentation or other accessible sources; preferentially cite documents accessible to the Search and Examination Section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial ARIPO search report when lack of unity (first-mentioned invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application does not comply with unity requirement, search and draw up a partial ARIPO search report for the invention (or linked group) first mentioned in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement the partial search report with a specification of the separate inventions. When determining which invention is first mentioned, take account of dependent claims but disregard trivial claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite documents relevant only to other inventions if basis for lack of unity a posteriori
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents relevant only to other inventions retrieved during the search on the first invention are not necessarily included in the partial search report unless they form the basis for a lack of unity a posteriori.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such documents must be cited in the partial search report if they form the basis for lack of unity determined after the search ('a posteriori').

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for lack of unity: refunds and authority for decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may contest non-unity and request refund of further search fees; the substantive Examiner decides on unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Examining Section finds contest justified the fees will be refunded. The criteria applied by the Search Examiner should be the same as those applied by the substantive Examiner. Search Section should not raise lack of unity merely because inventions are classified in separate units or to restrict search to certain documentation sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete search despite lack of unity when negligible additional work
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptionally, where further inventions can be searched with negligible additional work and cost, the examiner may make a complete search and prepare a search opinion for all inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all results in a single search report, raise the objection of lack of unity identifying different inventions, and indicate that the Search Section did not invite payment of further search fees because all claims could be searched without extra effort. The search opinion should still raise the issue of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary ARIPO search following an international application is based on first-mentioned invention
rubrics_metrics.description: In supplementary ARIPO searches after an international (PCT) search, the supplementary ARIPO search report will be based on the invention or group first mentioned in the claims serving as basis for the supplementary search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is done independently of the International Searching Authority's findings regarding unity of invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of methods for treatment and diagnostic methods (subject-matter excluded from patentability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy, and diagnostic methods practiced on the human or animal body, are excluded from patentability (subject-matter to be excluded from the search).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Products (substances/compositions) for use in such methods are not excluded provided the use is not comprised in the state of the art; 'Swiss-type' claims may be allowable for first or subsequent applications. Even if method claims are non-patentable, a meaningful search may be possible if the determining technical feature is the effect of the substance. If specific method features are present (dosing, combination with physical treatment) a meaningful search may not be possible. Regardless of whether such claims are searched, inform the applicant in the search opinion that such subject-matter is excluded from patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'meaningful' search and examples when no meaningful search possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a search is 'meaningful' is a question of fact for the Search and Examination Section; 'meaningful' should be construed reasonably (not merely because search is difficult).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples where no meaningful search may be possible: (i) claims lacking support/insufficient disclosure (broad/speculative claim supported by limited disclosure, making full search impossible or pointless); (ii) claims lacking conciseness (too many claims or possibilities making determination of protection unduly burdensome); (iii) claims lacking clarity (parameters chosen render comparison with prior art impossible). These examples are not exhaustive; basic principle is clarity and openness for applicant and third parties as to what has and has not been searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to indicate subject-matter for search when search impossible
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office considers the application does not comply with the Harare Protocol to such an extent that meaningful search is impossible for some or all claimed subject-matter, it will invite the applicant to file a statement indicating the subject-matter to be searched within two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invitation will give reasons for the finding and may indicate claimed subject-matter on which the Search Section considers it feasible to base a meaningful search.
